scenes.line1: How do you protect user data?
scenes.say: How do you keep user data safe, and what does GDPR mean for your code?

scenes.label: PII
scenes.sub: Personal data like names, emails, or addresses.
scenes.say: PII stands for personal data, like names, emails, or addresses. This stuff needs real protection.

rows.b: Limit who can see real data

scenes.say: First, spot the sensitive fields. Then, mask or encrypt them. Finally, make sure only the right people can see the real info.

scenes.title: Masking Email Addresses
scenes.say: Here's a quick example. We hide the start of each email, showing only the last five characters.

scenes.label: GDPR
scenes.sub: Requires consent, data minimization, and deletion.
scenes.say: GDPR is a privacy law. It means you need user consent, keep data minimal, and delete it if users ask.

scenes.question: Is masking enough for GDPR compliance?
scenes.wrong: Yes, masking covers all GDPR needs.
scenes.right: No, GDPR also requires consent, minimization, and deletion rights.
scenes.say: Don't fall for this trap. Masking helps, but GDPR also demands consent, data minimization, and the right to delete.
